title: Measuring Reading Fluency in Early Grades

text.Title 1: Measuring Reading Fluency in Early Grades

text.Content Placeholder 3:
Longitudinal cohort of 1,240 pupils across 38 primary schools followed from grade 1 to grade 3
Schools sampled to balance urban, suburban and rural catchments
Fluency measured three times per year with a validated one-minute oral reading task
Assessors blinded to intervention status and trained to a common standard
Primary outcome: words correct per minute at the end of grade 3

text.Text Placeholder 2: Small-group tutoring versus whole-class paired reading
text.Content Placeholder 3:
Small-group tutoring
Three 30-minute sessions per week led by trained teaching assistants
text.Content Placeholder 4:
Paired reading
Daily 15-minute sessions with peers matched by reading level

text.Text Placeholder 3: Both interventions improved fluency; tutoring helped struggling readers most

text.Content Placeholder 3:
Tutoring: +14 words correct per minute versus control
Paired reading: +9 words correct per minute versus control
Effects largest for pupils in the bottom quartile at baseline
No difference between urban and rural schools

Attrition of 11% by grade 3, higher in rural schools
Sensitivity analyses with multiple imputation gave consistent results
Next: a cost-effectiveness study with the regional education authority
Planned for the 2027–2028 school year
